chapters.title: The Computational Thinker
chapters.learn:
A computational thinker solves big problems the way a builder makes a robot: one small piece at a time.

Four super-skills

Decomposition – break a problem into small parts.
Pattern recognition – spot what repeats in numbers and shapes.
Abstraction – keep what matters, ignore the rest.
Algorithms – write clear steps anyone can follow.

Simple or difficult?

A simple problem has clear steps and one answer. A difficult problem has many choices, feelings or surprises, so we must break it down first.

questions.q: Which object is required to balance the last scale?
questions.hint: Use the second scale to compare a truck with cars.
s: The second row shows that 2 cars and 1 truck weigh the same as 2 trucks. So 1 truck weighs the same as 2 cars.
On the last scale, the 1 car and 1 truck on the left together weigh the same as 1 + 2 = 3 cars.
That leaves the bus on the left to be matched by a bus on the right. Answer: Bus.

questions.q: Identify whether the following everyday problems are Simple or Difficult.
items: a. Helping a friend who is feeling upset or worried.
b. Organizing our school bag before leaving for school.
c. Deciding what to do after missing the train.
d. Following a recipe to prepare a sandwich.
e. Finding a safe way home during heavy rain.
questions.hint: Simple = clear steps with one outcome. Difficult = many choices, feelings, or changing situations.
s: Simple problems have clear steps and one result: organizing a school bag (b) and following a recipe (d).
Difficult problems involve feelings, choices, or surprises: helping an upset friend (a), missing the train (c), and heavy rain (e).

questions.q: Study the pictograph (👧 = 2 students, half = 1). X = half of (Strawberries + Bananas). Y = Pears + Mangoes. Which fruit equals the difference between X and Y?
questions.hint: Turn each row of symbols into numbers first: full symbol = 2, half = 1.
s: Each full symbol = 2 students, half = 1: Strawberry = 12, Banana = 8, Pear = 9, Mango = 13.
Watermelon (X) = (12 + 8) ÷ 2 = 10 students.
Muskmelon (Y) = 9 + 13 = 22 students.
Difference = 22 − 10 = 12 students. The strawberry row has 6 full symbols = 12 students. Answer: Strawberry.

questions.q: Spot the pattern: What will come in place of '?' in the given series?
questions.hint: Look at each corner position separately from one square to the next.
s: Each number increases by 1 in the same position from one square to the next.
So [4, 5 / 5, 6] becomes [5, 6 / 6, 7]. Answer: d.

questions.q: Spot the pattern: What will come in place of '?' in the given series?
questions.hint: Check the top circle (+3), bottom circle (+1, +2, +3, +4...), and how they make the middle square.
s: Top circle: increases by 3 each time. After 15 comes 15 + 3 = 18.
Bottom circle: increases by 1, 2, 3, and 4. The next increase is 5, so 14 + 5 = 19.
Middle square: add the two circles (18 + 19 = 37). Answer: d (18, 37, 19).

questions.q: Find the ODD one out.
questions.hint: How do the two light numbers create the red number in three of the four groups?
s: In groups a, c, and d, the red number is the product of the two light boxes: 2×5 = 10, 7×4 = 28, 8×3 = 24.
In group b, 5 + 3 = 8 (it follows an addition rule instead of multiplication). Answer: b.

questions.q: An 8×8 land grid (each square = 30m × 30m) is split into Green (20 squares), Blue (23 squares), and Purple (21 squares), then redistributed equally. Which option does NOT represent land gained or lost by any house?
questions.vis:
Total = 64 squares × 900 sq.m = 57,600 sq.m → Equal share = 19,200 sq.m
Green: 20 sq (18,000) | Blue: 23 sq (20,700) | Purple: 21 sq (18,900)
questions.hint: Subtract each house's original area from 19,200 sq. m.
s: Each square = 30 × 30 = 900 sq. m. Total = 64 × 900 = 57,600 sq. m, so each house gets 57,600 ÷ 3 = 19,200 sq. m.
Green (20 sq = 18,000) gains 1,200 sq. m. Blue (23 sq = 20,700) loses 1,500 sq. m. Purple (21 sq = 18,900) gains 300 sq. m.
No house gains or loses 900 sq. m. Answer: d.

questions.q: Akash: minute hand at 12, hour hand 150° clockwise from it. Chirag: hour hand at 5, minute hand 210° clockwise from it. Which statement is correct?
o: a. Akash visited the park before Chirag
b. Chirag visited the park before Akash
c. Akash and Chirag visited the park at exactly the same time
questions.hint: Each step from one number to the next on a clock covers 30°.
s: Akash: 150° ÷ 30° = 5 steps clockwise from 12, so the hour hand is at 5 (5:00 p.m.).
Chirag: 210° ÷ 30° = 7 steps clockwise from 5, which lands on 12. Hour at 5, minute at 12 = 5:00 p.m.
Both visited at exactly 5:00 p.m. Answer: c.

questions.q: The printer connected to the computer is not responding. Tap the troubleshooting steps in the correct order (1 to 5).
items: Check that the printer has paper and enough ink or toner. Look for a paper jam or an error message.
If the printer still does not respond, restart both the printer and the computer, then print a test page.
Open the Print dialog box and make sure the correct printer is selected.
Make sure the USB cable is securely connected to both the printer and the computer.
Check that the printer is plugged in and switched on.
questions.hint: Start with the simplest physical check (power), then cable, software, consumables, and restart last.
s: Step 1: Check that the printer is plugged in and switched on.
Step 2: Make sure the USB cable is securely connected.
Step 3: Open the Print dialog box and choose the correct printer.
Step 4: Check paper, ink/toner, and jams.
Step 5: Restart both printer and computer, then print a test page.

chapters.title: The Power of Abstract Thinking
chapters.learn:
Abstraction means keeping the important details and ignoring the rest. A map does not show every leaf—only roads and landmarks.

Spatial & Visual Thinking

When rotating shapes, flipping mirror or water images, or finding 3D faces/edges/vertices, focus on key edges, corners, and directions.

Predict with Patterns

If numbers or jumps follow a steady rule, you can predict what comes next.

questions.q: Shoot (✕) exactly one item in each box. It is removed along with any identical items in adjacent boxes. What is the maximum number of items you can eliminate?
questions.hint: The middle box is adjacent to both outer boxes. Which shape appears in all three?
s: Left box: shoot Red Diamond (🔶) → removes 2 (left and middle).
Middle box: shoot Yellow Triangle (🔺) → removes 3 (one in each box).
Right box: shoot Pink Octagon (⬣) → removes 2 (middle and right).
Total: 2 + 3 + 2 = 7 items. Answer: d.

questions.q: Count the number of blocks that are connected to at least one smaller number and one larger number than the number in it.
questions.hint: Check only neighbours joined by a direct line.
s: Check each block's linked neighbours:
235 has 167 (smaller) and 410 (larger). 410 has 235 (smaller) and 453 (larger).
453 has 410 (smaller) and 579 (larger). 284 has 167 (smaller) and 831 (larger).
That makes 4 blocks. Answer: c.

questions.q: A school canteen recorded sandwiches sold over five weeks: Week 1: 100, Week 2: 125, Week 3: 150, Week 4: 175, Week 5: 200. How many will be sold in Week 6?
questions.hint: Look at how much sales grow from one week to the next.
s: Look at the gaps: 125 − 100 = 25, 150 − 125 = 25, and so on.
Sales increase by 25 sandwiches every week.
Week 6 = 200 + 25 = 225 sandwiches.

questions.q: Which option, when placed together with the given figure (touching without overlapping), will form a complete rectangle or square?
questions.vis: <svg viewBox='0 0 80 70' width='90' height='78' style='background:#fff;border-radius:10px;padding:4px'><polyline points='45,10 65,10 65,60 45,60 25,45 40,35 25,25 45,10' fill='none' stroke='#1d2a5b' stroke-width='4' stroke-linejoin='round'/></svg>
questions.hint: The given shape has one inward notch on the left. Look for the matching single outward-and-inward zigzag.
s: The zigzag edge of option a fits exactly against the zigzag edge of the given figure.
When the two pieces are joined, their straight outer edges form a complete rectangle. Answer: a.

questions.q: Fill in the number of Faces, Edges, and Vertices for each 3D shape.
questions.hint: Remember: a Sphere has 1 curved face and 0 edges/vertices; a Cylinder has 3 faces (2 flat + 1 curved) and 2 circular edges.
s: Cube & Cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices.
Cone: 2 faces, 1 edge, 1 vertex. Sphere: 1 face, 0 edges, 0 vertices.
Cylinder: 3 faces, 2 edges, 0 vertices. Square-based pyramid: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices.

questions.q: Sophia and her friends are flying over a town. Which top-view pattern matches Building B (slanted grey roof beside a small brown front wing)?
o: a. Grey vertical strip + brown top-right square
b. Grey left strip + brown lower-right rectangle
c. Grey left strip + brown upper-right rectangle
d. Grey & brown full side-by-side rectangles
questions.hint: Look straight down from above: the slanted grey roof forms a full left strip, and the brown wing sits at the lower-right.
s: From directly above, slopes appear flat.
Building B has the grey roof spanning the left side and the brown section at the lower-right. Answer: b.

questions.q: The given black-and-white pinwheel image can be rotated clockwise or anticlockwise. Which option CANNOT be obtained by rotating it?
questions.hint: Rotating a shape never flips its handedness (clockwise curl stays clockwise).
s: Options a, c, and d are 180°, 90° clockwise, and 90° anticlockwise rotations of the original.
Option b is mirror-flipped (reversed direction), so it cannot be obtained by rotation. Answer: b.

questions.q: Left box has blue square at bottom-left; right box has blue square at bottom-right. If both shift to the next corner clockwise, how will they look?
questions.hint: Clockwise corners go: Bottom-Left → Top-Left → Top-Right → Bottom-Right → Bottom-Left.
s: Left box: Bottom-Left moves 1 step clockwise → Top-Left.
Right box: Bottom-Right moves 1 step clockwise → Bottom-Left.
Result: [Top-Left, Bottom-Left]. Answer: d.

questions.q: Which option shows the correct mirror image (left ↔ right) of the clown face?
questions.hint: A vertical mirror flips left and right, NOT top and bottom—the party hat stays on top!
s: A mirror image keeps the top at the top and flips left ↔ right.
Only option b stays upright with left and right features mirrored. Answer: b.

questions.q: Which option shows the correct mirror image of the purple letter 'Q'?
o: d. Upright with tail pointing bottom-left
questions.hint: In a vertical mirror, a tail pointing bottom-right flips to point bottom-left.
s: The original 'Q' has its tail on the bottom-right.
Mirrored left ↔ right, it stays upright with the tail pointing bottom-left. Answer: d.

questions.q: An arrow points diagonally up-right (↗). Which option shows its correct water image (top ↔ bottom reflection)?
o: a. Arrow pointing down-right (↘) with reflected feathers
b. Arrow pointing down-right (↘) with reversed tip
questions.hint: A water image flips top and bottom, keeping left on the left and right on the right.
s: The tail stays on the left and the arrowhead stays on the right, while top flips to bottom.
So ↗ flips vertically to ↘ with matching reflected feathers. Answer: a.

questions.q: An upright triangle (△) has a horizontal line above it and 'W' inside. Which option shows its correct water image?
o: a. Inverted triangle (▽), line at bottom, wide 'M' inside
b. Inverted triangle (▽), line at bottom, narrow 'M' inside
c. Inverted triangle (▽), line at bottom, 'W' inside
d. Inverted triangle (▽), line at top, 'W' inside
questions.hint: Flipping top ↔ bottom turns △ into ▽, moves the top line to the bottom, and flips 'W' into 'M'.
s: In water reflection, the horizontal line moves from top to bottom and △ flips to ▽.
The letter 'W' flips upside-down to become 'M' with the same width. Answer: a.

questions.q: Figure A ([1, 4, _] / [2, _, 3]) is placed over Figure B ([_, 2, 3] / [_, 4, 1]) to form a 3×3 square grid. Which same digits will be positioned exactly on top of each other?
questions.hint: To form a 3×3 square grid from two 2×3 grids, place A's bottom row over B's top row!
s: Placing Row 2 of Figure A ([2, _, 3]) over Row 1 of Figure B ([_, 2, 3]) creates a 3×3 square grid.
In the right-most column, 3 sits directly on top of 3. Answer: b (3).

questions.q: A rabbit starts at −8 on this line: −12, −10, ⬜, −4, ⬜, 0 … 6, 8, … 14. It jumps to the 9th point right, then the 7th point left. What is the sum of all places it landed, including the start?
questions.hint: Each tick mark is 2 apart.
questions.review: Solution drafted by AI – needs approval.
s: From −8, 9 points right: −8 + (9 × 2) = 10.
From 10, 7 points left: 10 − (7 × 2) = −4.
Sum including start: −8 + 10 + (−4) = −2.
